subtopics.title: Water the Puller-Apart — Ions in Solution

questions.question: Water can dissolve ionic solids because the water molecule:
options: Is polar — a slightly negative oxygen end and slightly positive hydrogen end

questions.question: When sodium chloride dissolves, the oxygen ends of water molecules face:
Hydration is defined as:
options: The evaporation of water from a solution
The melting of an ionic crystal
Ions becoming surrounded by water molecules in solution

questions.question: The correct dissolution equation for table salt is:
An electrolyte is a substance whose solution:
options: Conducts electricity because it contains free ions

questions.question: Sugar solution leaves the tester bulb dark because sugar:
options: Dissolves as whole neutral molecules — no charge carriers

questions.question: Doubling the amount of dissolved salt makes the bulb glow brighter because:
options: There are more ions — more charge carriers — in the solution

questions.question: Conductivity is not always a measure of solubility because:
options: A substance like sugar can be very soluble yet produce no ions

subtopics.title: Precipitation — When Two Clear Solutions Make a Solid

questions.question: A precipitate is:
options: An insoluble solid that forms when two solutions are mixed

questions.question: The balanced equation for mixing silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions is:
The driving force of a precipitation reaction is:
options: One product escaping the solution as an insoluble solid

questions.question: Which compound from the Grade 10 short-list is soluble in water?

subtopics.title: The Ion Test Kit and the Four Reaction Types

questions.question: Nitric acid followed by silver nitrate gives a yellow precipitate. The ion present is:
The sulphate test uses nitric acid and:
options: Barium nitrate — a white precipitate insoluble in the acid confirms sulphate
Silver nitrate — a cream precipitate confirms sulphate

questions.question: A white precipitate with barium nitrate that dissolves in nitric acid with fizzing signals:
The fingerprint that identifies a redox reaction among the four types is:
options: Atoms changing charge because electrons are transferred

questions.question: The two ends of a water molecule are:
options: A slightly negative oxygen end and a slightly positive hydrogen end
A north pole and a south pole

questions.question: When salt dissolves, its ions are:
options: Pulled off the crystal and wrapped in escorts of water molecules

questions.question: Sugar's disappearing act differs from salt's because sugar molecules:
options: Break into positive and negative pieces
Float away whole and neutral — no ions form

questions.question: The label aq after an ion means it is:
options: Dissolved in water — swimming with a water escort

questions.question: In the tester, salt water lights the bulb because:
options: Free-swimming ions carry the current across the glass

questions.question: A dark bulb tells you:
options: That whatever dissolved carries no charge — not that nothing dissolved
That the water is pure enough to drink

questions.question: Brightness of the bulb keeps score of:
options: The concentration of ions in the solution

questions.question: Sports drinks advertise electrolytes because the body:
options: Needs sugar molecules for nerve signals
Runs nerves and muscles on ion traffic, and sweating loses ions

subtopics.title: Snow in a Glass — and Naming the Mystery Ion

questions.question: White snow appears when silver nitrate and salt solutions mix because:
options: Sodium and nitrate form a solid
Silver and chloride ions pair into insoluble silver chloride

questions.question: The splash of dilute nitric acid at the start of every ion test is there to:
options: Destroy any carbonate first, so it cannot fake another ion's white precipitate

questions.question: The halide traffic-light with silver nitrate reads:
options: Yellow chloride, white iodide, cream bromide
White chloride, cream bromide, yellow iodide
Green chloride, blue bromide, red iodide

questions.question: Partner-swap reactions differ from redox reactions in that partner-swaps:
options: Keep every ion's charge unchanged, while redox changes charges
